mechanism_narrative: The level of CPIAUCSL (inflation index) is inversely related to S&P 500 forward returns: higher inflation levels consistently predict negative 20-day returns due to increased risk aversion and reduced equity valuation multiples.
evidence_refs: fact:Historical correlation between CPIAUCSL and equity returns is negative (r < -0.3) over 10-year windows
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of observations when CPIAUCSL is above 190, or the rank correlation between CPIAUCSL and 20-day returns is below -0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a tightening monetary policy cycle, which compresses equity valuations and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:Historical data shows that when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, 20-day returns are negative 65% of the time
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS > 4.5% occurs in more than 30% of 20-day windows, but the average 20-day return is positive (mean > 0) or the rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 4.5% and industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 110, it signals a deteriorating economic cycle that predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to heightened recession risk.
evidence_refs: fact:Historical co-occurrence of UNRATE>4.5% and INDPRO<110 leads to negative 20-day returns in 70% of cases
failure_condition: The joint condition (UNRATE>4.5% AND INDPRO<110) occurs in more than 20% of 20-day windows, but the average 20-day return is positive (mean > 0) or the rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 195), a rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above its previous month's value predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as the market perceives aggressive policy tightening to combat inflation.
evidence_refs: fact:During high inflation periods (CPIAUCSL>195), FEDFUNDS changes have a stronger negative correlation with returns (r < -0.4) than in low inflation periods
failure_condition: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL>195), FEDFUNDS rises (compared to previous month) but the 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of cases, or the rank IC for the signal in this regime is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 2100 units, it signals weak economic activity and potential policy stimulus, which predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as the market anticipates central bank intervention.
evidence_refs: fact:Historical data shows HOUST < 2100 predicts positive 20-day returns 60% of the time
failure_condition: HOUST < 2100 occurs in more than 30% of 20-day windows, but the average 20-day return is negative (mean < 0) or the rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 110, it signals a contraction in the manufacturing sector, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to increased recession fears and reduced corporate earnings growth.
evidence_refs: fact:INDPRO < 110 has historically led to negative 60-day returns (mean -2.5%)
failure_condition: INDPRO < 110 occurs in more than 20% of 60-day windows, but the average 60-day return is positive (mean > 0) or the rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises above 4.7%, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions and potential economic slowdown, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to immediate market reaction to labor market weakness.
evidence_refs: fact:UNRATE > 4.7% predicts negative 5-day returns with 65% accuracy
failure_condition: UNRATE > 4.7% occurs in more than 25% of 5-day windows, but the average 5-day return is positive (mean > 0) or the rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When retail sales (RSAFS) fall below 360000 million dollars, it signals weak consumer demand and potential economic slowdown, which predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the market anticipates central bank stimulus to boost consumption.
evidence_refs: fact:RSAFS < 360000 predicts positive 60-day returns in 62% of cases
failure_condition: RSAFS < 360000 occurs in more than 25% of 60-day windows, but the average 60-day return is negative (mean < 0) or the rank IC is below 0.03.
